desc: On 9 September 2025 at 10:00 am in HVC-210 the House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna with Rep. Jasmine Crockett as ranking member, held 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'. The witnesses were Jeffrey Nuccetelli, a sixteen-year Air Force veteran who served in security forces at Vandenberg; Senior Chief Petty Officer Alexandro C. Wiggins, an operations specialist aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6); the journalist George Knapp; Dylan Borland, a former Air Force geospatial intelligence specialist; and, as minority witness, Joe Spielberger, senior policy counsel at the Project On Government Oversight. This is the hinge hearing of the modern era because it moved the enquiry from the phenomenon to the machinery. Nuccetelli testified to the 14 October 2003 Vandenberg incidents over missile defence sites, said each incident was 'witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated and reported up the chain of command', stated that 'official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI', and reported that a witness was threatened and told to keep quiet. Wiggins testified to 15 February 2023, approximately 7:15 pm PST, aboard USS Jackson: four self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped objects, one emerging from the ocean, holding formation and departing with near-instantaneous acceleration and no propulsion signature or sonic boom, recorded on the ship's Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system with timestamped data and reported to the tactical action officer. Knapp gave the most detailed public account yet of AAWSAP and BAASS: prime contractor status, roughly fifty investigators with top secret clearances, 27 months of operation, three dozen preliminary reports, over a hundred research papers, a 240,000-case data warehouse designed by Jacques Vallee that reportedly remains in agency use, and the fact that most of the papers remain unreleased by DIA. He also described James Lacatski's 2023 statement to DHS that the United States possesses a craft of unknown origin whose interior had been accessed, and the incomplete Bigelow-Lockheed material negotiation. Borland described a summer 2012 triangular craft observation at Langley AFB, alleged more than a decade of retaliation including blacklisting and clearance-record manipulation, and stated he had filed complaints with AARO in March 2023 and the Intelligence Community Inspector General in August 2023. The committee's two findings are the ones that matter: agencies withheld information from the Task Force, and UAP-related spending flows to entities outside the reach of the Freedom of Information Act. That second finding is the direct antecedent of Rep. Burlison's FY2027 NDAA amendment adopted on 23 July 2026, which extends disclosure obligations to government contractors. As of 12 August 2026 this remains the most recent congressional hearing devoted to UAP.

claims.text: The hearing 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' was held on 9 September 2025 at 10:00 am in HVC-210 before the House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.

The witnesses of record were Jeffrey Nuccetelli (U.S. Air Force Veteran), Chief Alexandro Wiggins (UAP Witness), George Knapp (UAP Journalist), Dylan Borland (UAP Witness, U.S. Air Force Veteran) and, as minority witness, Joe Spielberger, Senior Policy Counsel, Project On Government Oversight.

Knapp's written testimony is addressed 'Good morning, Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and Members of the Task Force', establishing Rep. Anna Paulina Luna as chair and Rep. Jasmine Crockett as ranking member.

Nuccetelli testified to five UAP incidents at Vandenberg Air Force Base between 2003 and 2005, stating: 'Each incident was witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated, and reported up the chain of command. We sent information up, but no guidance came down.'

Nuccetelli testified that the 14 October 2003 incursion began 'when Boeing contractors reported a massive, glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites', and that 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI.'
Nuccetelli testified that after a subsequent Vandenberg incident 'The witness was later threatened and told to kept quiet about the incident, discouraging further reports.'

Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer (Operations Specialist) with approximately 23 years of service, testified to an event on 15 February 2023 at approximately 1915 PST in the W-291 warning area off Southern California aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6), involving a self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped object emerging from the ocean, linking up with three similar objects, and departing simultaneously with no sonic boom or conventional propulsion signature.

Wiggins testified that the event was recorded inside the Combat Information Center on a Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system, that 'The released, stabilized footage includes timestamps, lat/long, and platform readouts consistent with USS Jackson's location in W-291 at the time of the encounter', that the objects were held on radar, and that reports were made to the Tactical Action Officer.

Knapp testified that BAASS, the prime contractor for AAWSAP, 'managed to recruit and hire fifty full-time investigators for BAASS, most of them former military or law enforcement, and all of whom were able to qualify for top-secret security clearances.'

Knapp testified that in its 27-month existence AAWSAP/BAASS produced 'more than three dozen preliminary reports (DIRDs)' and a data warehouse of 'more than 240,000 case files', which 'was designed and overseen by Dr. Jacques Vallee and has reportedly been used by U.S. agencies up to the present date.'

Knapp testified that AAWSAP/BAASS 'also produced more than 100 highly detailed papers focusing on different issues and questions, including studies of the health effects on humans from encounters with UFO/UAP technology. None of these 100-plus reports have been released by DIA, though a few have been leaked.'

Knapp testified that during Kona Blue discussions with a US senator and an undersecretary of the Department of Homeland Security, Dr. James Lacatski revealed that 'the U.S. is in possession of a craft of unknown origin and had successfully gained access to its interior', with 'a streamlined configuration suitable for aerodynamic flight but no intakes, exhaust, wings, or control surfaces.'

Knapp testified: 'I have confirmed that Bigelow and a trusted colleague met with and negotiated with a senior executive at Lockheed and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that Lockheed was safeguarding at a facility in California. A source who was in the room for that discussion has confirmed this.' He added that the material's 'composition suggested it had been crafted in a zero-gravity environment' and that 'The agreement was not completed.'
Knapp stated on the record that 'Mr. Grusch now works for Representative Burlison as an advisor on these matters.'

dossier.denialPosture: No Department of Defense, AARO or DIA witness appeared and no departmental response to the hearing's custody claims - Air Force records held by AARO and the FBI, unreleased DIA papers, the Lockheed material negotiation - has been published. The Department's standing position, restated in AARO's annual reporting, remains that it has found no verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial technology; it has not addressed the specific documentary and contractual allegations made under oath at this hearing.
dossier.narrative:
The Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets is a creature of the 119th Congress, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, and it exists because the 2023 and 2024 hearings demonstrated that a standing subcommittee without access to compartments could not move the file. The 9 September 2025 hearing was held in HVC-210, a House Visitor Center room, with five witnesses and written statements posted by the committee.

Jeffrey Nuccetelli, a former Air Force military police officer with sixteen years of active duty, testified to five UAP incidents at Vandenberg Air Force Base between 2003 and 2005 - the home, as his statement notes, of the National Missile Defense Project, during launches described by the National Reconnaissance Office as 'the most important in twenty-five years.' His formulation of the oversight failure is exact: 'Each incident was witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated, and reported up the chain of command. We sent information up, but no guidance came down.' The 14 October 2003 incursion - Boeing contractors reporting 'a massive, glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites' - is the incident Rep. Luna had raised at the 2023 hearing, and Nuccetelli states that 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI.' That is a custody claim with two named holders. He also testified that after a later incident 'The witness was later threatened and told to kept quiet about the incident, discouraging further reports.'

Alexandro C. Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer with roughly twenty-three years of service, gave the hearing its hardest sensor evidence. On 15 February 2023 at approximately 1915 PST, in the W-291 warning area off Southern California, aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6), a self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped object was observed emerging from the ocean, joined three similar objects, and all four departed simultaneously with no sonic boom and no conventional propulsion signature. The event was recorded from the Combat Information Center on a Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system with visible time and location stamps, the objects were held on radar, and reports were made to the Tactical Action Officer. His statement is careful about what the data does and does not show, and notes an approximate altitude reference of about 22,000 feet reflected in CIC operator conversation.

George Knapp's written testimony is the document that makes this hearing structurally important. He describes AAWSAP as conceived by DIA's Dr. James Lacatski and a colleague, funded through Senator Harry Reid and two other senior senators, and contracted to Robert Bigelow's BAASS, which 'managed to recruit and hire fifty full-time investigators for BAASS, most of them former military or law enforcement, and all of whom were able to qualify for top-secret security clearances.' In twenty-seven months the programme produced 'more than three dozen preliminary reports (DIRDs)' and 'compiled the largest known UFO database - or rather data warehouse - consisting of more than 240,000 case files obtained from multiple other collections, including files from other governments.' That warehouse 'was designed and overseen by Dr. Jacques Vallee and has reportedly been used by U.S. agencies up to the present date.' The programme also produced 'more than 100 highly detailed papers', of which 'None of these 100-plus reports have been released by DIA, though a few have been leaked.'

Knapp then puts two custody claims on the record. First, Lacatski's 2023 statement during Kona Blue discussions with a US senator and an undersecretary of the Department of Homeland Security that 'the U.S. is in possession of a craft of unknown origin and had successfully gained access to its interior', described as having 'a streamlined configuration suitable for aerodynamic flight but no intakes, exhaust, wings, or control surfaces.' Second, and more concrete: 'I have confirmed that Bigelow and a trusted colleague met with and negotiated with a senior executive at Lockheed and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that Lockheed was safeguarding at a facility in California. A source who was in the room for that discussion has confirmed this.' The material 'contained no unknown element, no unobtanium, but its composition suggested it had been crafted in a zero-gravity environment.' And then: 'The agreement was not completed.'

Knapp also notes, almost in passing, a fact that matters for how this file is now being worked: 'Mr. Grusch now works for Representative Burlison as an advisor on these matters.' The 2023 whistleblower is now congressional staff support on the same subject.

The Russian half of Knapp's testimony - Ministry of Defence documents from his 1993 and 1996 Moscow visits, Colonel Boris Sokolov's decade-long standing collection order 1978-1988, General Igor Maltsev's standing order to disengage, the October 1982 Ukraine missile base incident in which launch displays illuminated and could not be shut down - is presented as material already handed to AAWSAP and BAASS for analysis, with the resulting report 'included in one of those unreleased papers submitted to DIA and still bottled up there.'

The minority witness, Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight, was there for whistleblower protection rather than phenomena, which is the correct read of the hearing's title. The Task Force's theory is that the bottleneck is not evidence but the legal exposure of the people who hold it.
openQuestions: Whether AARO and the FBI in fact hold the Vandenberg 2003 records Nuccetelli names, and whether either has been asked for them in writing by the Task Force.
The identity of the Lockheed Martin senior executive who negotiated the BAASS material transfer, the California facility involved, and why the agreement was not completed.
Whether the AAWSAP 240,000-case data warehouse designed by Jacques Vallee is still operational, in which agency's hands, and under what contract.
The disposition of the more than 100 unreleased AAWSAP/BAASS papers held by DIA, and whether any FOIA or committee request for them has been answered.
Whether the USS Jackson Star SAFIRE source video and radar tracks were ever transmitted to AARO, and whether the case was adjudicated.
Dylan Borland's testimony was not obtained for this dossier and his written statement has not been reviewed here.
dossier.whatItIs: A hearing of the House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, held 9 September 2025 at 10:00 a.m. in HVC-210, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna with Rep. Jasmine Crockett as ranking member, titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'. The witnesses were Jeffrey Nuccetelli, Senior Chief Petty Officer Alexandro C. Wiggins, George Knapp, Dylan Borland, and minority witness Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the hearing at which the enquiry stopped being about lights in the sky and became about programme architecture, contracts and custody. Knapp's written testimony placed on the congressional record a detailed account of AAWSAP/BAASS as a prime-contract intelligence programme - fifty cleared investigators, twenty-seven months, a 240,000-case data warehouse still reportedly in agency use, more than a hundred papers never released by DIA - and an account of a negotiated transfer of anomalous material from Lockheed Martin to a private contractor that was agreed and then not completed. Nuccetelli testified that documented, investigated UAP incursions over the National Missile Defense sites at Vandenberg produced records now held by AARO and the FBI, and that a witness was threatened into silence. Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief, put multi-sensor Star SAFIRE EO/IR imagery of a transmedium object into the record with time, coordinates and platform. Taken together the hearing establishes that the material, the records and the contracts are locatable - and that the committee could name where they sit without being able to compel their production.

entityInfo.desc: Beyond the headline moments, the 9 September 2025 record contains three further items worth preserving. Burlison entered into the record witness testimonies supplied to him by Dr. Steven Greer, naming Michael Herrera, Roderick Castle, Randy Anderson and Steven Digna among others. Burlison also stated on the record that the UAP Disclosure Act 'was stripped out by the House last year, and I cannot get it onto the bill leaving the House this year,' which is the House-side counterpart to the Senate story of the UAPDA's gutting. And Ranking Member Crockett placed the whole subject inside the documented history of American overclassification - MLK and Malcolm X, COINTELPRO, the torture programs - which is the framing that makes the inquiry survivable across party control.

timeline.label: Luna task force declassification push
timeline.text: The House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets lists UAP and unidentified submerged objects among its declassification priorities and requests an administration update.

timeline.label: Operators testify: Wiggins, Nuccetelli, Borland, Knapp
timeline.text: The Task Force hearing seats an active-duty Navy senior chief describing a sensor-recorded encounter, two Air Force veterans, and a journalist. Wiggins: 'that is first and foremost a safety issue.'

timeline.label: Third House UAP hearing
timeline.text: The Task Force hears Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and Spielberger in HVC-210; Biggs, Begich, Ogles, Titus and Moskowitz are waived on.

timeline.label: Task Force hearing on UAP transparency and whistleblower protection
timeline.text: Crane enters the reprisal letter into the record; George Knapp tells the Task Force from the witness table that extra-legal reprisals against Grusch were occurring in recent days; Nancy Mace states his medical information was leaked to discredit him. Grusch attends but does not testify.

timeline.label: Lockheed Martin named on the record, with an executive
timeline.text: George Knapp testifies that Bigelow negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives for material held in California that 'was not made here'; tells Rep. Burchett that Lockheed is one of the holders and offers a list; and names Dr. James Ryder at Lockheed and Glenn Gaffney of CIA as gatekeepers.

timeline.label: The hinge hearing
timeline.text: Luna's Task Force hears Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland; the committee finds agencies withheld information and that UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach. Witnesses say AARO holds unreleased video.

timeline.label: Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets holds its UAP whistleblower hearing
timeline.text: Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna convenes 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' in HVC-210 with witnesses Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and minority witness Spielberger. Rep. Crane submits a letter to the Secretary of Defense on the Grusch reprisal. Printed as Serial No. 119-44 (CHRG-119hhrg61718).

timeline.label: The Task Force turns to the machinery
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland testify. The committee finds agencies withheld information and that UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach. Nuccetelli names AARO and the FBI as custodians of Vandenberg records.

timeline.label: House Task Force hearing on UAP transparency
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland testify. Wiggins is the first active-duty Navy official to do so publicly. Borland describes retaliation. Witnesses tell the Task Force AARO holds additional video records. Burlison presents drone-versus-orb footage from Yemen.

timeline.label: House Oversight Task Force hears five UAP witnesses
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and Spielberger testify in HVC-210. Rep. Burlison plays previously unseen video of an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024; the object appears struck and not destroyed.
